S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: Two years and four months before psychiatric care, Shirley was promoted to oversee a larger quality-improvement portfolio across several clinics, including EPIC reporting, bilingual community-access metrics, and more cross-functional meetings than she had ever managed at once. Her previously effective systems of color-coded calendars, late-night spreadsheets, and coffee-fueled catch-up sessions gradually stopped compensating: she struggled to stay with long analytic tasks, missed key points in direct conversations, left reports and committee follow-ups unfinished, avoided dense policy-review work, and repeatedly misplaced badges, notes, and files needed for meetings. The problem became clinically significant when delays began affecting clinic deadlines and also spilled into her volunteer health-workshop planning, prompting her to use her organization’s employee assistance referral for a psychiatric evaluation.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: What finally pushed me to come in is that I can start an EPIC quality report or sit down in a clinic metrics meeting with every intention of tracking it, and within a few minutes my mind has drifted so far that I’m rereading the same numbers or realizing I missed the whole point of the discussion.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: When a medical director or one of my coordinators is talking directly to me, I’ll be looking at them and nodding, but then I have to ask them to repeat the action item because the words just didn’t stay with me.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: If someone gives me three or four follow-up steps after a committee meeting, I may do the first one and maybe draft the second, but then the email, spreadsheet, or final submission sits unfinished until someone reminds me.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: I find myself putting off the dense policy reviews and long data-analysis blocks until late in the day, because the thought of sitting with that much detailed reading and thinking feels almost physically hard to start.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m constantly hunting for the badge, handwritten notes, clinic folders, or even the flash drive I just had in my hand before a meeting, and it’s embarrassing because I used to be the organized one.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Even in elementary school, I remember teachers writing that I was bright but careless, and my mother had to sit with me while I finished homework because I would lose track of assignments or forget books at school.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: At work, my delays have started affecting clinic reporting deadlines and making other teams wait on me, and I’ve had to step back from leading parts of the volunteer health workshops because I can’t reliably keep the planning pieces moving.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on since my promotion about two years and four months ago, when the larger portfolio started overwhelming the systems I used to rely on.
